skill_drafts.name: Maven Project Initialization
skill_drafts.description: Quick-start workflow to set up a new Maven project from scratch, covering project structure, archetype selection, and initial configuration within 5–30 minutes.

applicable_signals: Onboarding a developer to Maven basics
Need to establish standard project structure

Apply the archetype to generate the project skeleton
Verify standard directory layout is created (src/main/java, src/test/java, etc.)

skill_drafts.name: Maven Dependency Resolution
skill_drafts.description: Workflow to declare, manage, and resolve project dependencies using Maven's dependency mechanism, including optional dependencies and exclusions.
skill_drafts.objective: Manage and resolve project dependencies correctly
applicable_signals: New library or framework requirement identified
contraindications: Do not use for resolving transitive dependency conflicts at runtime
Do not use for debugging repository connectivity issues
Do not use for managing repository mirrors or authentication
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify the dependency to add or modify', 'detail': 'Determine groupId, artifactId, and version from the library documentation or Maven Central Repository'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Declare the dependency in pom.xml', 'detail': 'Add a <dependency> block in the <dependencies> section with groupId, artifactId, and version'}

{'step': 3, 'action': 'Apply optional or exclusion rules if needed', 'detail': 'Mark dependency as <optional>true</optional> if it should not be transitive, or add <exclusions> to block unwanted transitive dependencies'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify dependency resolution', 'detail': 'Run Maven dependency tree command to confirm all dependencies resolve correctly and no conflicts remain'}

Updating an existing dependency version
Excluding transitive dependencies to resolve conflicts
Marking a dependency as optional

Dependency coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version) must be correct
Maven must have access to configured repositories
cautions: Excluding too many transitive dependencies may break functionality
Optional dependencies still require explicit declaration in dependent projects
Version conflicts in transitive dependencies may require additional exclusion rules
output_contract: pom.xml with correctly declared dependencies, optional flags, and exclusion rules; successful dependency tree resolution with no unresolved or conflicting dependencies

metadata.prompt: Use this skill when you need to add, update, or configure dependencies in a Maven project. Verify the dependency tree resolves correctly after configuration.

skill_drafts.name: Maven Build Lifecycle Execution
skill_drafts.description: Execute Maven build phases in proper sequence, understanding phase dependencies and orchestrating the complete build lifecycle from compile through deploy.
skill_drafts.objective: Execute Maven build phases in proper order with all prior phases completed
applicable_signals: User initiates mvn command with lifecycle phase target
Build requires validation of phase execution order
Downstream artifacts depend on prior phases completing
contraindications: Configuring individual plugin goals or plugin-specific behavior
Debugging plugin execution failures or plugin parameter issues
Customizing site generation or documentation build steps
workflow_steps: Identify the target lifecycle phase (compile, test, package, verify, install, deploy)
Confirm all prerequisite phases will execute in order
Execute the Maven command targeting the desired phase
Monitor phase completion and artifact generation
Verify all expected build artifacts are produced
triggers: Running a Maven build from command line or CI/CD pipeline
Understanding phase dependencies before customizing build order
Need to execute specific lifecycle phases or full build sequence
constraints: Phases must execute in Maven's defined sequence
All prior phases in the lifecycle must complete before later phases
Phase execution is atomic within the lifecycle context
cautions: Skipping phases may result in incomplete builds or missing artifacts
Phase execution order cannot be reordered; it is fixed by Maven's lifecycle definition
output_contract: Successful execution of the requested lifecycle phase(s) with all prior phases completed; build artifacts generated and available for downstream use or deployment.

metadata.prompt: Invoke this skill when you need to run a Maven build and ensure all lifecycle phases execute in the correct order. Maven's build lifecycle consists of phases that must run sequentially: validate, compile, test, package, verify, install, and deploy. Use this skill to understand which phases are executed, their dependencies, and how to target specific phases or the full lifecycle.

contraindications: Troubleshooting runtime errors
Debugging plugin execution during active builds
Modifying plugin behavior mid-build cycle
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Create or verify Maven project directory structure', 'details': 'Ensure src/main/java, src/test/java, src/main/resources, and src/test/resources directories exist; place pom.xml at project root'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Define POM project coordinates and metadata', 'details': 'Set groupId, artifactId, version, name, description, and packaging type in the POM'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Configure dependencies in POM', 'details': 'Add required dependencies with scope (compile, test, provided, runtime) and version specifications'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Set up build profiles', 'details': 'Define profiles for different build scenarios (e.g., dev, test, prod) with activation conditions and profile-specific configurations'}

{'step': 7, 'action': 'Validate POM and settings', 'details': 'Check XML syntax and structure; run mvn validate to confirm POM correctness'}

Migrating an existing project to Maven
Reconfiguring project structure and build profiles
constraints: POM file must be valid XML
Project coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version) must be defined
Directory structure must follow Maven conventions
cautions: Ensure all dependencies are available in configured repositories before proceeding to build
Validate profile activation conditions to avoid unintended build variations
Review plugin versions for compatibility with the target Java version
output_contract: Valid POM file with correct project descriptor, profiles, and plugin configurations ready for build execution. The project structure conforms to Maven conventions, all dependencies are declared, and the POM passes validation.

metadata.prompt:
Follow these steps to set up and configure a Maven project:
1. Create or verify the project directory structure with src/main/java, src/test/java, and pom.xml at the root.
2. Define the POM file with project coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version), packaging type, and dependencies.
3. Configure build profiles in the POM to support different build scenarios (e.g., development, testing, production).
4. Set up plugin configurations in the POM for compilation, testing, and packaging.
5. Review the Settings descriptor to ensure repository and credential configurations are correct.
6. Validate the POM syntax and structure before proceeding to build execution.

skill_drafts.name: Local Repository JAR Installation
skill_drafts.description: Install third-party or custom JAR files into the local Maven repository with correct groupId, artifactId, and version metadata for project dependency resolution.
skill_drafts.objective: Register a JAR artifact in the local repository
applicable_signals: Adding a non-Central Repository JAR to project dependencies
Integrating legacy, proprietary, or locally-built artifacts
Resolving missing artifact errors for unavailable remote sources
contraindications: Artifact is already available in Central Repository
Artifact is available in a configured remote repository
Standard dependency declaration in POM is sufficient
workflow_steps: Identify the JAR file path, groupId, artifactId, and version
Execute mvn install:install-file with -Dfile, -DgroupId, -DartifactId, and -Dversion parameters
Verify artifact appears in local repository at ~/.m2/repository/[groupId]/[artifactId]/[version]/
Add dependency declaration to project POM and confirm resolution without errors
triggers: Adding a non-Central Repository JAR (legacy, proprietary, or local build) to project dependencies
constraints: JAR file must exist and be accessible at specified path
groupId, artifactId, and version must be provided and valid
Local repository directory must have write permissions
cautions: Ensure groupId and artifactId match project naming conventions to avoid resolution conflicts
Verify JAR integrity before installation to prevent runtime classpath errors
output_contract: JAR file installed in local repository at correct hierarchical path; POM dependency declaration resolves without download errors; artifact is available for project compilation and runtime classpath

metadata.prompt: Use the Maven install:install-file goal to register a JAR artifact in the local repository. Provide the JAR file path, groupId, artifactId, and version. Verify the artifact is placed at the correct path in the local repository and that subsequent POM dependency declarations resolve without download errors.

skill_drafts.objective: Register external JAR artifact in local repository

Integration of vendor-supplied or custom JAR
contraindications: Artifact already available in Central Repository
Artifact should be deployed to shared remote repository for team access
Dependency is managed by a corporate artifact repository

Proprietary or non-standard library integration needed

Group ID, artifact ID, and version must be known or inferred
Local repository must have write permissions

To install a third-party JAR to the local Maven repository:

5. Run a test build to confirm the dependency resolves without download attempts.

Invoke this skill when you need to run a Maven build and ensure all lifecycle phases execute in the correct order. Maven's build lifecycle consists of phases that must run sequentially: validate, compile, test, package, verify, install, and deploy. Use this skill to understand which phases are executed, their dependencies, and how to target specific phases or the full lifecycle.

## Objective

Execute Maven build phases in proper order with all prior phases completed
## Applicable Signals

- User initiates mvn command with lifecycle phase target
- Build requires validation of phase execution order
- Downstream artifacts depend on prior phases completing

## Contraindications

- Configuring individual plugin goals or plugin-specific behavior
- Debugging plugin execution failures or plugin parameter issues
- Customizing site generation or documentation build steps

## Workflow Steps

- Identify the target lifecycle phase (compile, test, package, verify, install, deploy)
- Confirm all prerequisite phases will execute in order
- Execute the Maven command targeting the desired phase
- Monitor phase completion and artifact generation
- Verify all expected build artifacts are produced

## Constraints

- Phases must execute in Maven's defined sequence
- All prior phases in the lifecycle must complete before later phases
- Phase execution is atomic within the lifecycle context

## Cautions

- Skipping phases may result in incomplete builds or missing artifacts
- Phase execution order cannot be reordered; it is fixed by Maven's lifecycle definition

## Output Contract

- Successful execution of the requested lifecycle phase(s) with all prior phases completed; build artifacts generated and available for downstream use or deployment.

Establish reproducible build configuration
## Applicable Signals

- Project requires deterministic build output
- Multiple environments must produce identical artifacts
- Compliance or audit requirements demand reproducible builds

## Contraindications

- Debugging single-run builds where environment variation aids diagnosis
- Build environment-specific variation is intentional or required
- Rapid prototyping where build consistency is not a priority

- Review current Maven pom.xml and settings.xml for environment-dependent properties
- Document all build parameters: compiler version, plugin versions, dependency versions, timestamps
- Configure reproducible build properties in pom.xml (e.g., project.build.outputTimestamp)
- Update settings.xml to enforce consistent repository mirrors and credentials handling
- Execute build in first environment and capture artifact checksums
- Execute build in second environment and verify artifact checksums match
- Document reproducible build configuration and validation results

- Maven configuration must be version-controlled
- All build properties must be explicitly declared in pom.xml or settings.xml
- Build output must be validated across at least two independent runs

## Cautions

- Reproducible build configuration may conflict with dynamic dependency resolution; pin versions explicitly
- Timestamp and build metadata must be controlled to avoid non-deterministic output

## Output Contract

- Maven configuration (pom.xml, settings.xml) with reproducible build properties documented and validated across test runs. Artifacts produced in different environments must have identical checksums.
